sources.title: Intent Docs
sources.locator: Getting Started; Workspaces; Agents & Chat; Context; Git & Code Changes; Home; Multi-device support; Intent mobile; Sharing Workspaces; Settings; Token Savings; Support
sources.finding: Free desktop app (macOS; Windows/Linux alpha). Workspaces are created by picking a GitHub repo, copying a local git repo into a worktree, or initializing a new git repo. Controls include secret requests via hidden input (opt-in), ask-before-using-tools, usage-limit retry on another provider. Notes support tags and anchored comment threads; Cmd+K searches note contents across workspaces. Home lists workspaces in list or board view grouped by Needs you/Running/Done & idle, filters All/Needs you/Running/Archived, group by repository or detailed PR status, shows each workspace status message, a Pull requests tab for PRs you created/were assigned/asked to review, and Fleet HUD. Changes panel shows PR CI checks and agents can monitor PRs for comments and CI. Transfers include notes, conversations, workspace assets and the git repository; event history, terminals and running processes stay on the source. Mobile app shows diffs and exports diagnostic logs. Sharing: invite links (expiring or pinned to one GitHub/GitLab account), Participant and Manager roles, discussions with @mentions, People panel, guests can leave. New workspaces start with one agent by default. Token view shows input/output/cached/reasoning tokens per agent; costs appear when the provider reports them. Support: file a GitHub issue; bugs that can be verified are fixed.

sources.title: Intent README (pinned)
sources.locator: What is Intent? (L37-L40); Supported agents (L59); How it works (L82); Network & privacy (L113)
sources.finding: Claude Code runs with a Claude subscription or API key, Codex with a ChatGPT subscription or API key; local models run on your own hardware. Intent does not proxy or resell model access; compute is your laptop, your machines, E2B sandboxes or your own VMs. Apache 2.0, local-first, no product analytics or crash reporting. Clients are thin JSON-RPC clients of the intentd Rust daemon; each agent gets its own MCP bridge so agents can edit the spec, delegate, message each other and run scripts, and every action is attributable; each workspace gets an isolated copy-on-write checkout on its own branch. Components: Electron + SvelteKit desktop app, SwiftUI iPhone/iPad app (private repo). Network access is limited to update checks (anonymous update statistics on by default, with a Settings toggle and env/config opt-outs), user-initiated provider sign-ins, and user-configured GitHub (OAuth device flow or PAT), Linear (API key), Sentry (API token) and MCP servers.

sources.title: Intent backend architecture (pinned)
sources.locator: Daemon overview L18-L50; L214-L222; Local models L371; Hooks L476-L536; Agent process-tree memory L874-L925
sources.finding: The daemon exposes an MCP server back to its own agents with a per-agent bridge address so tool calls are attributable; an optional context engine shells out to auggie when available. Until the local node ships, agents not placed remotely share the workspace checkout. The unsloth provider runs Unsloth GGUF models locally through a daemon-managed server. Agent-authored hooks run with a 60 s wall-clock budget; perpetual hooks re-arm until TTL expiry; schedules persist in SQLite and rehydrate at boot, healing running rows back to scheduled. agents.maxConcurrent is a concurrency cap, not a resource cap; idle reaping and an auto RAM-derived memoryBudgetMb evict idle process trees; process-tree memory is reported via system.status.

sources.title: Protocol §8 Permission Flow (pinned)
sources.locator: Implementation status and Default policy (L13-L41); normalized payload; outcomes (L71)
sources.finding: The daemon mediates ACP session/request_permission requests: interactive policy blocks the agent stream and surfaces the prompt with allow_once/reject_once options and a heuristic riskLevel; unanswered prompts time out after 5 minutes as cancelled. Shipped default policy is AllowAll (bypass mode); Interactive, AutoByRisk and DenyAll are selectable via INTENTD_PERMISSION_POLICY.

sources.title: Protocol §5.48 Multiplayer (pinned)
sources.locator: Method table L28-L54 (members.remove, invite.revoke, revokeSelf); Workspace guest roles L43-L90; Invite links L174; Join step 5 L208; Revocation L218; Workspace transfer L863
sources.finding: Workspace roles are owner, collaborator (shown as Participant) and manager; the owner can remove members and revoke invites, guests can leave or revoke all their credentials, and invites expire after 7 days by default (max 30). Guests reach the shared workspace by connecting to the host daemon through its tunnel route. Presence is a roster layered on membership (§5.47). Workspace export carries default discussion history but not named or private conversations.
